title: 🎙️ A Tiny Model That Understands You in 40 Languages — and Rivals Giants 60 Times Its Size!
body: 🎙️ A Tiny Model That Understands You in 40 Languages — and Rivals Giants 60 Times Its Size!

Company Reason 8 released its Ramble 2 Flash model as open-source software under the Apache 2.0 license on November 18 — a speech-recognition model with just 0.5 billion parameters that understands more than 40 languages and detects the language automatically.

Despite its small size, the model achieved an average error rate of 6.96% on the multilingual track of Hugging Face's open speech-recognition leaderboard, beating OpenAI's Whisper Large v3 and Meta's Omni ASR, which is 15 times larger — and the company says it rivals models 3 to 60 times its size.

The model is also extremely fast: it processes a full hour of audio in about half a second when batches are full — more than 7,000 times real time — and at just 1.39 GB, it runs on a laptop or local server without your audio ever leaving your device.

The model works directly with the popular Transformers and vLLM tools with no custom code, and the company also offers it via a cloud service starting at 0.01 euros per hour of audio — noting that some features, such as speaker recognition, are reserved for the larger Ramble 2 model.

Simply put: imagine a small, lightweight assistant that hears and understands you in any language, writes down your words faster than the big players, and lives on your own device rather than in a distant cloud — that is Ramble 2 Flash.
Would you prefer a small open model that runs on your device, or a huge model in the cloud?
